clue.text: Religious claim is thrown out

indicators.note: something thrown out of shape is knocked into disarray, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's religious claim has been dismissed out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown out' reads like a rejection of the claim, but it is telling you to jumble the two words that precede it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic describes things belonging to the faith of Islam, so it is one particular kind of religious adjective.

clue.text: Written avoiding rules? Trainee penning lie mostly needs attention

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
to pen is to enclose, as sheep are penned, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: an intern is a trainee, especially in medicine
the word with its last letter cut off
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A note about a trainee, distracted by a fib, who needs supervising and writes off the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruled lines on writing paper are the 'rules': interlinear text sits between them rather than on them, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlinear text is inserted between the printed lines of a page, so it ignores the ruled lines in a playful sense.

clue.text: Remaining airlines' business losing following

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: what airlines do is fly passengers
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An airline company is shedding its loyal followers or its remaining trade.
explanation.walkthrough: F for 'following' is the abbreviation used in page references (pp. 10f). Take it from FLYING to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying somewhere is staying put there, as in snow lying on the ground, so remaining is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Preserved meat given up by one who can tell the future is fish

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

parts.note: ham is cured, preserved pork

parts.words: one who can tell the future
parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller renounces cured meat and declares fish the thing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given up' sounds like abstaining from meat; in a down entry it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The mahseer is a large freshwater game fish of South Asian rivers, related to the carp.

clue.text: Principal uneasy over scheme, something governing body moves

parts.note: principal means main or central
uneasy means anxious, on edge
a scheme is a plan or method of organisation

explanation.surface: A head teacher is anxious about a plan, an idea that will steer how the governors act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' and 'governing body' suggest a school; the governing body is really the human body, and 'over' places the first two words above the third in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain and spinal cord form the control centre that sends the signals making muscles move the body.

clue.text: Where one may find hot spices — hot not cold — readily

indicators.note: saying one thing and not another means this letter is used in place of that one

parts.words: Where one may find hot spices
parts.note: hot spices are found in a curry
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cooking note about where the hot spices go, delivered quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A CURRY is where spices end up; swap its C (cold) for H (hot), the letters on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something readily means doing it promptly and without delay, which is acting quickly or with haste.

clue.text: Cardinal's twiddling a sort of chain

indicators.note: twiddling is fiddling and twisting about, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A cardinal fidgets with his chain of office or rosary.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as plain letters, not a possessive or 'is'. 'Chain' suggests a rosary; it is a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An island arc is a curved line of volcanic islands formed above a subduction zone, a chain in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Attacked caterpillar always will escape the onset initially

indicators.note: initially points at the start of each word, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A caterpillar under attack will always get away before the assault begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The aweto is a New Zealand caterpillar killed by a parasitic fungus that grows out of its body, hence 'attacked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aweto is the larva of a moth infected by Cordyceps fungus, so it is literally a caterpillar under fungal attack.

clue.text: I shush rep being unruly in director's office

indicators.note: unruly means out of control, so the letters will not stay in their given order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quietens an unruly sales rep who has barged into the boss's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director's office' suggests a room; it means the post itself, and an usher directs people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Usher is one who shows people where to go, and -ship names the position held, so this is the post of a director.

clue.text: Potato disease resistance in being acquired protects tuber finally

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written
got means obtained or acquired

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A potato disease takes hold despite resistance, with only the tuber finally protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' and 'tuber' look like part of the plant-disease story; they supply R twice, once as the physics symbol and once as a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring rot is a bacterial infection of potatoes that leaves a ring of decay inside the tuber, so it names a specific potato disease.

clue.text: Weaken one politician with broadcast

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A single politician going on air could undermine their own position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is not an anagram signal here; it is a straight synonym, as in airing a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or diminish its strength or quality, which is to weaken it.

clue.text: Inventor surrounded by old stuff set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it, so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to be in something is to be surrounded by it
O is the abbreviation for old
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: An inventor lives buried among old junk he has piled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by' looks like a container instruction but simply supplies the word IN; the whole string is then written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian inventor credited with developing long-distance radio telegraphy.

clue.text: Gross rage is out of order for assailant

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extreme anger is unacceptable behaviour from someone who attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as the British idiom for unacceptable conduct, but literally tells you to disorder the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the person who launches an attack first, so an assailant is a close synonym.

clue.text: Brilliant place to finish in here, avoiding pressure

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within a larger word
avoiding something means doing without it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to be here is to be present
P is the symbol for pressure
Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A boast that ending up here, free of stress, is a brilliant place to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESENT loses its P, and PL plus END go inside what remains. Pl. is how Place is abbreviated in British street addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendent means dazzling or splendidly bright in appearance, a close synonym of brilliant in its shining sense.

clue.text: What leads to colours in fall? Crown cover around New York has northeast eclipsing south

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece encloses another
to eclipse is to blot out and replace from view, so one letter covers over and supplants another

parts.note: to trip is to fall
a helmet covers the crown of the head
the standard abbreviation
taken as written
the compass abbreviation
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: An autumn question about leaves changing colour, followed by a garbled tale of a hat in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colours in fall' invites American autumn foliage; fall is simply TRIP. Has becomes HANE when NE takes the place of S. The word 'has' is doing double duty as wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Triphenylmethane is the parent hydrocarbon of a large family of synthetic dyes, so it is the chemical that gives rise to colours.

clue.text: Hearing organ's part in tango make sweet backing

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is written from end to start

parts.note: to sugar something is to sweeten it

explanation.surface: Part of a dance band's backing track is sweetened to please the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part in' suggests a hidden word, but there is none; the definition is the whole opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The tragus is the small cartilage flap in front of the ear canal, a part of the outer ear.

clue.text: Clear damage on electronic component with direct oscillation

parts.note: simple means plain, clear and easy to understand
harm is damage
taken as written
IC is an integrated circuit, an electronic component
to motion someone is to direct them by a gesture

explanation.surface: An engineer clears up the damage to a part that sets things swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic component' is two words for two letters, IC, the integrated circuit. 'Direct' is a verb: you motion someone to a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple harmonic motion is the regular to-and-fro movement of a pendulum or spring, the idealised form of oscillation in physics.

clue.text: Rascal with Irish accent, not British

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a brogue is a lilting accent, typically Irish
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A charming scoundrel speaks with an Irish lilt that is clearly not British.
explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is a strong regional accent, usually Irish; drop its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a mischievous or dishonest but often likeable person, which is what a rascal is.

clue.text: Managed most of palace retinue's resentment

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a royal court is a palace retinue, here missing its last letter

explanation.surface: Most of the royal household has come to share a festering grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'retinue's' is padding for the surface; court is the household of attendants around a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or ill will, a long-lasting form of resentment.

clue.text: One only separating in Louisiana to annoy Louis XIV

indicators.note: to separate something is to come between its parts, so one piece splits another apart

parts.note: roil is the chiefly American form of rile, so it is how you annoy someone in Louisiana
sole means only, as in the sole survivor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone Frenchman in Louisiana sets out to irritate the Sun King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Louisiana' tells you to use the American verb roil, meaning to rile; Louisiana was itself named after Louis XIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Roi Soleil, the Sun King, was the nickname of Louis XIV of France, who took the sun as his emblem.

clue.text: Bury Malian unclothed among other things

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped bare, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: to inter is to bury
the word with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A burial custom from Mali, among other things, involves stripping the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the English town but is a verb. A Malian is someone from Mali in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is the Latin tag used in English to mean among other things, signalling an incomplete list.

clue.text: Time to acquire? Save up for washing machine

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to win something is to acquire it

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned around

parts.note: save means except, as does but

explanation.surface: Shopping advice: is it time to buy, or should you save up for a new washer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like saving money, but it means except, as in 'all save one'. A twin-tub is an older British washing machine with one tub to wash and one to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is a type of washing machine with separate drums for washing and spin-drying, popular in Britain before automatics.

clue.text: Current EU politician getting round popular old chancellor

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to get round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
something hot is fashionable and in demand

explanation.surface: A sitting Euro MP wins over a well-liked former finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old chancellor' suggests a past German or British finance minister; Imhotep was chancellor to the Egyptian pharaoh Djoser around 2650 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Imhotep served as chief minister or chancellor to Pharaoh Djoser and designed the Step Pyramid at Saqqara.

clue.text: Balkan region once badly run with imam regularly ignored

parts.note: illy is a rare adverb meaning badly
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means skipping every other letter and keeping the rest

parts.note: the first and third letters, with the second and fourth skipped

explanation.surface: An old Balkan territory was poorly governed, its religious leaders often overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly run' looks like an anagram signal, but 'badly' gives the archaic adverb illy and 'run' gives R separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was the ancient region along the eastern Adriatic coast, in what is now the western Balkans.

clue.text: Playwright capturing all the rage about mad cow disease

indicators.note: capturing something means taking it in and holding it, so one piece encloses another
about here means around, so the outer piece is placed on either side

parts.note: something in is fashionable
BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A dramatist cashes in on the BSE scare, writing a fashionable play about mad cows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the rage' sounds like fury, which suits madness, but it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist behind A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: After a change to the final ordering, goes out live

indicators.text: After a change to the final ordering
indicators.note: changing the order at the end means the closing letters swap places

parts.note: one who goes out exits

explanation.surface: Following a late reshuffle, someone leaves while still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters move; everything before them stays where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive or to have being, so it fits live as an intransitive verb.

clue.text: Falls around church? It can put one's arm out

definitions.text: It can put one's arm out

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: trips are falls
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles near a church and dislocates an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's arm out' suggests dislocation; it is meant literally, as straightening the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps muscle at the back of the upper arm extends the elbow, pushing the forearm outwards.

clue.text: Typical EU out of control — they have branches in Australia

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so the letters break out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at a chaotic EU, with branch offices even in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests company offices; it means the boughs of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti are gum trees, native to Australia, and as trees they literally have branches.

clue.text: Included map showing home station

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to station something is to set or place it

explanation.surface: A guidebook comes with a map pinpointing the local railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' suggests a railway stop; it is the verb meaning to place.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small map placed within the border of a larger one, so it is a map included in another.

clue.text: Hertfordshire village a short way east of railway

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped
in an across entry east is to the right, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: an el is an elevated railway in American cities
a street is a way, here with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: Directions to a village a little way east of the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree, north of London, is famous for its film and TV studios. EL for railway is borrowed from American usage, as in Chicago's El.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is a village in the English county of Hertfordshire, just north of London.

clue.text: Carpets woven in ranges of colour

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rugs are woven in a wide palette of hues.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is so natural that 'woven' reads only as a weaving verb, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is the full band of colours light splits into, so spectra are ranges of colour.

clue.text: Dog — retired always going after right one

indicators.note: to go after something is to follow it, so this piece is placed later in the line

parts.note: ret. is the abbreviation for retired
R is the abbreviation for right
I is the Roman numeral one
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A dog in retirement still follows its master faithfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Ret. is the standard abbreviation for retired, as after an officer's name; 'going after' places the always-word behind the right-one pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a breed of gun dog trained to fetch shot game, such as the Labrador or golden retriever.

clue.text: Indian dish of husked bran with fat

indicators.note: husking strips off the outer casing, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the inside of the word
the inside of the word
the inside of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe for an Indian dish of husked bran cooked in fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husked' seems to apply only to bran, but it applies to all three words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cool yoghurt side dish from the Indian subcontinent, often with cucumber and mint.

clue.text: Check bank document's replacement

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a bank statement lists an account's transactions

explanation.surface: A customer checks the bank's statement after a replacement was issued.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition. 'Check' sounds like a cheque, which suits the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstatement means putting someone or something back in a former position, so it is replacement in the sense of restoring.

clue.text: Fit to grasp English acting

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it tight, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a person in trim is in good shape, or fit
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone is fit enough to get to grips with English drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' sounds like the stage; it means temporary, as in an acting head.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim manager holds a post temporarily, which is what acting means in a job title.

clue.text: Perhaps blight turned some of the rose yellow

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters read from right to left
some of means a portion only, so the letters come from inside a run of words

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A gardener suspects disease has turned a rose yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blight' suggests plant disease, which suits the rose; here it means an ugly sight, as a building can be a blight on the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight on the landscape is something ugly that spoils it, and an eyesore is an example of that.

clue.text: Still show nave vault a bit damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so its letters are put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The church roof is slightly damaged but still on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning 'even now'; it is an adjective, motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a scene posed by silent, motionless actors, literally a living picture, so a show that stays still.

clue.text: An exchange of words travelling on last train

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters shift into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Two passengers have words with each other on the last train home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An exchange of words' suggests an argument; it means swapping words of one language for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Translating replaces each word of one language with an equivalent in another, a literal exchange of words.

clue.text: Work on and off switch for siren

parts.note: to temp is to do short-term office jobs intermittently
a switch is a hairpiece, a tress of false hair

explanation.surface: Instructions to work a switch that turns a warning siren on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On and off switch' looks like one phrase, but the split falls after 'off'. A switch is a long lock of false hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of myth lured sailors with song, so a siren is a seductive woman, a temptress.

clue.text: Grand mushrooms rising broad and flat, billions must be about

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upwards, so the word reads backwards
one thing must be another means it is to be replaced by it

parts.note: ceps are porcini mushrooms
tabular means flat like a table top
B is the abbreviation for billions
c. is the abbreviation for circa, about

explanation.surface: A cook marvels at a grand display of mushrooms sprouting broad flat caps by the billion.
explanation.walkthrough: TABULAR has its B swapped for C. 'About' is c. for circa, as in c.1900, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectacular is impressive and showy on a large scale, which is what grand means in this sense.

clue.text: Note falsehoods going about like false names

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: lies are falsehoods
as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: A warning that lies are circulating, as fake names tend to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going about' reads as spreading around, but it means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used to hide identity, so aliases are false names.

clue.text: Raid home with dogs inside having eaten nought

indicators.note: having eaten something means having swallowed it, so one piece ends up held within another

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
curs are mongrel dogs
in means inside
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A burglary at a house where the dogs indoors had been given nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs inside' suggests one piece goes inside another; instead 'inside' is a separate word giving IN, and that IN eats the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a sudden hostile invasion of territory, a short attack much like a raid.

clue.text: Civil engineer needs resistance in a soil to settle

indicators.note: in means placed within, so these letters go inside another word

parts.note: to soil is to stain
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An engineer needs to know how firm the ground is before it settles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like earth, which suits the engineer; it is the verb to dirty. 'Settle' means determine, as in settling a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, and settling a question likewise means establishing the answer definitively.

clue.text: Bound to harvest green buds

parts.note: to cut a crop is to harvest it
capers are the pickled green flower buds of a Mediterranean shrub

explanation.surface: A worker is obliged to pick the young green buds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'Bound' is the definition, a leap, and 'to' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut capers is an idiom for leaping and frolicking about playfully, so it matches bound as a verb meaning jump.

clue.text: Rain beats violently, but one's staying dry

indicators.note: violently means with wild force, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rain lashes down, yet one person somehow stays dry.

explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller is said to be dry, so someone who abstains from alcohol is a person staying dry.

clue.text: Make amends towards an individual

parts.note: at means directed towards, as in aim at
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put things right with a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as one instruction, but it splits into the definition and two short words joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a wrong done, which is what making amends means.

clue.text: Woollen footwear perhaps is striking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knitted coverings for the feet

definitions.note: a verb phrase where the answer is a third-person verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: hits hard with a punch

explanation.surface: A fashion comment that knitted footwear is eye-catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like an adjective, eye-catching; it is the verb, hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks are typically woollen foot coverings, and to sock someone is slang for punching them.

clue.text: Noticed millions doing evil in place of deal making?

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, to notice
M is the abbreviation for millions
ill means evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Someone spotted millions being made crookedly where business deals are struck.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British term for softwood timber, so a deal-making place is where planks are cut; the question mark flags the pun on business deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawmill cuts logs into planks, and deal is fir or pine timber, so it is literally where deal is made.

clue.text: Son Tommy upset about papa's sign of disease

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes on either side of another
upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'papa's' links to the definition as 'is'. The jumbled name splits round the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a physical or mental feature indicating a condition, so it is a sign of disease.

clue.text: Fanatical about knight with a female to worship

parts.note: mad about something is fanatical about it
on means about, as in a book on birds
N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with a knight and his lady love, who is to be adored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanatical about' reads as one phrase, but each word is its own piece. N for knight avoids confusion with K for king in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is the Virgin Mary, venerated in Christian worship, and the name also suits the pop star with devoted fans.

clue.text: Thrilled about a ram for religious ritual

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to be sent is to be thrilled or transported
taken as written
to ram things in is to cram them in

explanation.surface: Worshippers are excited about a sacrificial ram for a holy rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' looks like the animal, which suits a ritual; it is the verb to force in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a Christian rite such as baptism or communion, so it is a formal religious ritual.

clue.text: Spider scuttled to end up under article

indicators.note: in a down entry being under something means coming after it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to scuttle is to run hurriedly

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading bottom to top, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A spider scurried off only to end up beneath an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End up' looks like an idiom for finishing somewhere, but 'up' turns the end-word upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Araneid is the zoological term for any spider, from Araneae, the order containing all spiders.

clue.text: Point to a missile advanced across river bank

indicators.note: to lie across something is to straddle it, so one piece spans either side of another

parts.note: ahead means advanced, further forward
R is the abbreviation for river
